label: associative-conditioning-03-recovery
supersedes: conditioning-02 remains the qualified no-recovery run; this re-runs the identical battery with the version-2 recovery term
cue_selection: Among twelve candidate keys cue:A..cue:L probed on unit gains (seed 17, plasticity off), the pair with the lowest KC-set Jaccard among cues with at least 400 active KCs and 60 MBON05 spikes: cue:E (411 KCs; MBON05 60, MBON01 53) and cue:F (473 KCs; 73, 67), Jaccard 0.128. Conditioning-01 used cue:A/cue:B with Jaccard 0.39, whose overlap produced large generalization.
readout_justification: Plasticity-off sensitivity measurement on cue:A: setting every eligible gain to 0.5 reduced MBON01 by 55% (85 to 38) and MBON05 by 29% (90 to 64); both are the natural appetitive-memory MBONs, so the summed count of both learned compartments is the primary response readout. Gain criteria remain per compartment.
backward_justification: Dopamine before the cue is predicted by the declared rule and by Handler et al. 2019 to potentiate, an opposite-sign effect; conditioning-01 treated it as a null and its predicted potentiation (+0.082 mean A-edge gain) then masked the paired depression (-0.089). A directional control cannot define the null scale.
interpretation: Controlled cue learning on the actual MaleCNS graph with an engineered optogenetic-style reinforcer of the sugar-reward dopamine neurons. Passing establishes acquisition, retention, reversal and dopamine dependence for this simulator, not natural sugar reward, feeding or sports usefulness.

additional_criteria.no_gain_above_rest: every eligible gain <= rest_gain at every endpoint
additional_criteria.paired_differs_from_unpaired: already required by the 3x null criterion
additional_criteria.recovery_reported: total recovery term per arm reported
